newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened mildly against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies following Bank of Israel intervention to support the basket, dealers said.
"The market was quiet today. Once again the Bank of Israel intervened only when the basket fell below the lower range of the trading band," said one dealer.
"In late morning the central bank intervened on a low scale, but just before the setting of the representative rate it started buying on a larger scale," he added.

"The shekel declined against the dollar as the dollar rose abroad following the U.S. air strike in Iraq. When the dollar slipped from earlier highs the shekel rose mildly," a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank said.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against the basket, representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1480 against 3.1440 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5416 shekels against 3.5402 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8834 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8823 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1175 shekels per mark against 2.1210 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1480 shekels.
